messages.author: 62a7fe14c0ce6d79
messages.subject: procD.pgls
parts:
Hello - is procD.pgls only to be used with coordinate data? (eg coords ~ size)?
It seems to work well for other types of data, such as tests for size allometry in a single PC component (eg Comp1 ~ size) or multiple PC components (eg Comp1:Comp20 ~ size) or even for categorical variables (eg coords ~ Diet, or Comp1 ~ Diet). But is procD.pgls appropriate for these uses?

Also, I've noticed that results for continuous or categorical univariate tests often differ significantly from those using gls() with a corPagel or Brownian correlation, but perhaps this is simply because procD.pgls and gls differ so much in their approach?

Thanks
Faysal

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] procD.pgls
parts:
Faysal,

all ANOVA/regression-type tests in geomorph base their significance testing in the residual permutation procedures. They are in fact based on wrapping more general (i.e. not specific to GM coordinates) functions of the RRPP package. As such, they can be used for any kind of data for which regression-type approaches are correct, and they are bound to differ from other approaches precisely because they assess significance in a whole different way.

For more details, I suggest you read the function's help files, and Collyer, M. L. and D. C. Adams. 2018. RRPP: RRPP: An R package for fitting linear models to high‐dimensional data using residual randomization. Methods in Ecology and Evolution. 9(2): 1772-1779. https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/2041-210X.13029

Antigoni

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] procD.pgls
parts:
Faysal,

 

A quick comment on the second portion of your email.

 

If one implements things correctly – and uses the same model choices (e.g., BM and lambda = 1 for both) - procD.pgls and ML-based PGLS via gls() should yield equivalent results.

 

This was demonstrated in Adams and Collyer 2018 (Evolution) for phylogenetic ANOVA. The Supplemental Information of that paper shows things empirically via simulation:  see Supp. Figs 1-2 for beta and F-values being identical, and p-values differing only due to the number of permutation iterations.  Also, Figs S4-S6 in that same SI demonstrate that the empirical F-distribution from RRPP in procD.pgls is identical to the distribution from theory.

 

This property also holds for phylogenetic regression.

 

Dean
